The Digital Egypt Youth (DEY) initiative plays a vital role in achieving one of the strategic objectives of the ICT sector by empowering young Egyptians to thrive in the digital economy, contributing to the country’s socioeconomic development and digital transformation initiatives. The Digital Egypt Youth (DEY) initiative aims to provide young Egyptians with the necessary skills and knowledge to thrive in the digital age. The initiative focuses on training youth in various digital fields to increase their employability and entrepreneurship opportunities. It specifically targets young Egyptians, equipping them with in- demand skills needed for jobs in the digital economy, and aims to bridge the digital skills gap in Egypt to create a digitally skilled workforce supporting the country’s digital transformation.

The initiative offers a full-fledged scholarship and targets 2,500 fresh graduates from Egyptian universities nationwide. The initiative adopts an upskilling approach covering two aspects: technical upskilling and personal/soft-skills upskilling, seeking to cover various digital skills to cater to diverse interests and career paths. DEY collaborates with industry partners and experts to develop and deliver relevant training content, ensuring the program aligns with industry requirements and equips participants with practical, in-demand skills. The program facilitates job placement by partnering with industry stakeholders, creating linkages between trained individuals and potential employers through one month of on-the-job training at the industry partner’s premises. NTI has collaborated with more than 75 national and multinational industry partners — including Amazon (AWS), Etisalat Egypt, Vodafone, Huawei, WE, Cisco, VMware, Orange, Valeo, Avelabs, SEITech, Brightskies, and VOIS, among others — to design more than 30 professional tracks that meet job profiles and ICT market needs. At the end of the program, participants receive joint certification from NTI and the industry partners, validating their skills and competencies for future job opportunities. Category: Electronics and Embedded Systems 4.1 Digital IC Design — Code: E004 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours Overview

Introduces students to digital electronics design and implementation on FPGAs (architecture, digital design flow, Verilog coding guidelines), with hands-on projects for basic digital blocks and complex FPGA implementations. Covers timing violations and power analysis using ISE & Vivado IDEs on Zynq-7000 development kits. Also covers ASIC design methodology (cost/size reduction through miniaturization and integration) and RTL-to-tape-out conversion, plus verification engineering: constructing a robust verification plan and complex UVM test cases for SoC designs. Prerequisites Good knowledge of digital electronics design. Basic knowledge of HDL languages (VHDL/Verilog). Basic knowledge of FPGA and ASIC technology. Contents Module 1: Digital Design with FPGA Digital systems design review; top-down digital design flow; introduction

of FPGA and ASIC technology. Contents Module 1: Digital Design with FPGA Digital systems design review; top-down digital design flow; introduction to FPGAs and FPGA architecture; FPGA flow overview; ultrafast design methodology; VHDL/Verilog motivation, modules, operators, combinational/sequential logic; simulators; hierarchical design; blocking vs non-blocking assignments; test-benches; functions/packaging/tasks; compiler directives; system tasks; finite state machines; design constraints; timing analysis; FPGA tool design flow; Project 1 (UART); scripting languages. Module 2: Digital Design ASIC ASIC introduction; STA basics and timing paths; FF requirements and timing constraints; EDA tool design objects; logic synthesis; formal verification; synthesis tutorial and project; floor planning, power planning, placement, ICC; CTS, routing, chip finishing; complete synthesis/formal

verification; synthesis tutorial and project; floor planning, power planning, placement, ICC; CTS, routing, chip finishing; complete synthesis/formal verification/PNR/STA tutorial (2 parts); extraction and STA; EMIR and power estimation; final project. Module 3: Digital Design Verification Verification basics; System Verilog (data types, process blocks, hierarchical structures, compiler directives, scheduling, assignments, classes, randomization, coverage); UVM overview, hierarchy, base classes, factory, phasing, resources/configurations, TLM, sequences/sequencers, components, full environment, UVM testing lab; Design for Testability (DFT). Hands-On: Labs using FPGA kits (e.g., Zynq-7000); writing VHDL/Verilog and System Verilog programs. 4.2 Electronics Design for Industry — Code: E006 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours Overview

writing VHDL/Verilog and System Verilog programs. 4.2 Electronics Design for Industry — Code: E006 Technical Program Duration: 294 Hours Overview Prepares hardware designers capable of developing complete, production-ready electronic designs for smart devices (washing machines, water heaters, meters, access controls, cars, etc.). Targeted skills: design/simulation tools, sensors and actuators, linear and switched-mode power supplies, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), PCB tools, thermal design, and reliability/lifetime estimation. Prerequisites Basic knowledge of circuits. Basic analytical skills. Basic knowledge of statistics. Contents Basic Electronic Design (96 hr): Circuit simulation (LTSpice — transient, AC, DC, parametric, Monte Carlo); ADC types, performance, limitations; transducers and actuators; analog signal conditioning and filter design; op-

AC, DC, parametric, Monte Carlo); ADC types, performance, limitations; transducers and actuators; analog signal conditioning and filter design; op- amp circuits (amplifiers, active filters, level shifters, instrumentation, multi-vibrators, log, rectifiers) with practical limitations; oscillators; galvanic isolation; protection (ESD/HBM, transient protection, MOV/TVS selection); comm buses (RS232/422, I2C, SPI, UART, CAN); practical transistor circuits (BJT, MOS switches, relay drivers); heat sink sizing.

Power Supply Design (96 hr): Switching-mode power supply basics; passive/active component parasitics; non- isolated and isolated DC/DC converter design; inductor/transformer design; EMI filter design; efficiency analysis. PCB Design for Manufacturing & EMC (96 hr): PCB design tool, component management, layer stack and layout, library/reuse; Design for Manufacturing (DFM) — manufacturing processes, reliability/lifetime calculations; Design for EMC — concepts and standards, conducted/radiated emission and immunity (setup, mechanisms, mitigation), PCB EMC design guidelines (board structure, digital/analog/high-speed/high-voltage, shielding). Hands-On: Sensor interfacing/calibration labs; PCB design tool; 10W flyback power supply design lab; EMC labs (conducted emission evaluation); power supply lifetime estimation. 5. NTI Summer Training Program National Telecommunication Institute (NTI) & ITIDA — Egypt Source: https://www.nti.sci.eg/summertraining/ Program Overview The Summer Training initiative is a joint program between the National Telecommunication Institute (NTI) and the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA), under Egypt's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT). It aims to train and qualify Egyptian university students in the pre-graduation stage, building their capabilities in modern, high-value technological fields. Target students: First, second, and third-year students from faculties of Engineering (Computer & Systems, Communications, and Electronics departments), Computers & Information, Artificial Intelligence, as well as Business Information Systems (BIS) & Business Informatics.

The program is a free scholarship for outstanding Egyptian undergraduate students, selected according to each track's conditions. It is delivered both online and in person, at NTI premises and at Digital Egypt Innovation Hubs (Creativa) across Egypt's governorates. The program is part of a national push to train 10,000 students. Graduates receive a certificate accredited by both ITIDA and NTI, along with preparation opportunities for international certifications and hands-on, real-world simulation projects.
